newsitem.title: CANADA: French newspaper in Quebec City backs Liberals.
newsitem.headline: French newspaper in Quebec City backs Liberals.

text.p: The French-language daily newspaper in Quebec City, home of the secessionist Quebec provincial government, has thrown its support behind the Canada's ruling Liberal Party in the June 2 federal election.

The endorsement is conditional, however. In an editorial on Tuesday, the newspaper Le Soleil said it hopes party leader and current Prime Minister Jean Chretien will step down before finishing his next mandate, assuming he wins the election.
Le Soleil praised the Liberals for their progress in reducing Canada's budget deficit and strengthening the nation's finances.
"The Liberal party of Canada has proved its determination in this area, and it has more experienced national team to govern the country than it did in 1993," the paper said.
"Nonetheless, we hope the party's leader, Jean Chretien, will give up his position to a new face before the end of his mandate. Quebeckers would grateful and so would his party."

The Liberals face a tight three-way race in mainly French-speaking Quebec against the separatist Bloc Quebecois and the Conservative Party. While the Liberals have a slight edge in the polls, Chretien, a native of Quebec, is widely unpopular in his own province.
Le Soleil rejected support for the Bloc Quebecois, saying the it was not an effective opposition in Ottawa because it was too preoccupied with promoting Quebec sovereignty.
